scraped.scraped_description: OpenSanctions helps investigators find leads, allows companies to manage risk and enables technologists to build data-driven products.

name: OpenSanctions
tagline: Supreme Data on Supreme Leaders - open source sanctions and politically exposed persons data platform
sdg_alignment: SDG 16 – Peace, Justice and Strong Institutions
dependency_risks: Reliance on 330 external data sources for accuracy and timeliness
Data quality dependent on source reliability
Potential for data duplication or conflicts across sources
awards: Transparency International Award for Data Innovation
policy_outcomes: Adoption by financial institutions for AML/KYC compliance
Use by NGOs for sanctions monitoring
outcome_methodology: Case studies and user adoption tracking
documented_limitations: Data extraction from free text sources prone to LLM errors including dropped middle names and hallucinated details
jurisdictional_scope: Global - integrates data from 330 sources including UN Security Council sanctions, national sanctions lists, and criminal databases
failure_modes: Inaccurate entity matching leading to false positives in screening
Lag in data updates affecting real-time compliance
Incomplete coverage of emerging sanctions regimes
governance_model: Open governance with community contributions and advisory board oversight
curation_criteria: Data meets quality standards for screening systems and investigative use; de-duplicated and cleaned through open source data pipeline
contributor_governance: Open contribution model with code review and data validation processes
controversies: Individuals have requested removal from database; deletion policy published but contested
Inclusion of Russian company data from 2022 prompted questions about data completeness and political framing
political_bias_allegations: None formal; database reflects official government sanctions designations which may themselves carry geopolitical bias
legal_regulatory_issues: GDPR-relevant data on individuals; privacy policy and deletion request process published; operates under German law
ai_involvement: LLM-based text extraction for entity identification from free text sources, with human moderation
political_relevance_summary: OpenSanctions addresses the civic need for government transparency and open data access, enabling citizens, journalists, and researchers to hold public institutions accountable.

movement_building_utility.notes: OpenSanctions provides foundational data infrastructure, standards, or platforms that other civic technology efforts build upon.

generalizability_notes: High generalizability. OpenSanctions is open source and already deployed across multiple countries/jurisdictions, making replication straightforward for other contexts.
